predictions.title: Inkling lands as a hyperscaler managed fine-tuning tier by Q2 2027
predictions.body: Thinking Machines released Inkling on July 15 as its first from-scratch model — a 975B-total / 41B-active Mixture-of-Experts trained on 45 trillion multimodal tokens, published as open weights with a 276B Inkling-Small preview alongside. The release is explicitly not pitched as the strongest model available; the bet is that enterprises want a customizable base they can fine-tune rather than a rented frontier endpoint, and the weights route directly into Tinker, the company's paid fine-tuning platform. The distribution pattern around the launch is the tell: Together AI served Inkling on day 0 behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and Unsloth landed same-day support in v0.1.49-beta, so the third-party serving and tuning stack formed within the news cycle. The big-3 clouds already compete on the breadth of their managed fine-tuning catalogs, and a frontier-scale open-weights base whose entire commercial identity is fine-tunability is precisely the artifact those catalogs onboard. The prediction is that at least one big-3 hyperscaler lists Inkling or Inkling-Small as a first-party managed fine-tuning target — not merely raw hosting — by Q2 2027, turning Thinking Machines' fine-tune-first release strategy into shelf placement inside a hyperscaler's enterprise customization product.

reasoning.because: Inkling shipped as open weights built for fine-tuning, with day-zero Together and Unsloth support
reasoning.given: Big-3 clouds already run managed fine-tuning catalogs and compete on open-weight model breadth
reasoning.so_that: At least one big-3 hyperscaler onboards Inkling or Inkling-Small as a first-party managed fine-tuning target
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; ≥1 big-3 cloud lists Inkling in its managed fine-tuning catalog
reasoning.plain_language: A big AI lab gave away its huge model so companies can retrain it; soon a major cloud will sell that retraining as a service.

predictions.summary: Inkling, the 975B open-weights MoE Thinking Machines built to be fine-tuned rather than rented, drew day-zero support from Together AI and Unsloth. Because big-3 clouds compete on managed fine-tuning breadth, at least one will onboard Inkling or Inkling-Small as a first-party tuning target by Q2 2027.

predictions.title: Microsoft breaks Patch Tuesday's monthly cadence for AI-surface fixes by Q2 2027
predictions.body: Microsoft will split its AI surfaces out of the monthly Patch Tuesday rhythm and ship them on a faster-than-monthly security servicing cadence. The July 14 release fixed a record 570 vulnerabilities, and the striking part was not just the volume but the composition: a critical remote-code-execution flaw in Microsoft Copilot itself (CVE-2026-48561), a GitHub Copilot RCE, a Copilot/VS Code security-feature bypass, and a Copilot/VS Code token-disclosure flaw — the assistant and its host editor now form a recurring vulnerability category rather than an exotic one-off. Microsoft attributes the record volume to its own AI-powered internal vulnerability-discovery system, which means the pipeline producing these findings will keep accelerating, and Adobe responded to the same pressure the same day by moving to twice-monthly bulletins, citing AI-accelerated discovery compressing the window between disclosure and exploitation. A monthly batch cycle designed for operating-system components sits badly on cloud-updated assistants whose flaws are found continuously and weaponized quickly; Copilot fixes largely deploy server-side anyway, so the engineering cost of decoupling them is low while the exposure cost of holding them for a monthly train keeps rising. The prediction is that Microsoft formalizes this: either a publicly documented accelerated cadence for Copilot-class services or a dedicated AI-surface security servicing channel, announced by Q2 2027.

reasoning.because: Record 570-CVE Patch Tuesday included a critical Copilot RCE plus three more Copilot/VS Code flaws
reasoning.given: AI-assisted discovery compresses disclosure-to-exploit windows; Adobe already moved to twice-monthly
reasoning.so_that: Microsoft ships a faster-than-monthly security servicing channel for Copilot and other AI surfaces
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; Microsoft announces faster-than-monthly Copilot security cadence
reasoning.plain_language: Hackers and defenders both use AI to find bugs faster, so Microsoft will start shipping Copilot security fixes more often than once a month.

predictions.summary: Copilot and VS Code flaws are now a recurring Patch Tuesday category, and AI-assisted discovery is inflating CVE volume while shrinking exploit windows. Adobe already went twice-monthly. Microsoft follows by Q2 2027 with a faster-than-monthly security cadence for its AI surfaces.

predictions.title: TSMC 2nm node climbs to 20% of wafer revenue by Q2 2027
predictions.body: TSMC's second-quarter 2026 results put the 2-nanometer node at 3% of wafer revenue in its first meaningful quarter, inside a record print — US$40.20 billion in revenue, up 36% year-over-year, with net income up 77.4% and a 67.7% gross margin. The prediction is that 2nm repeats the trajectory its predecessor traced: 3nm debuted as a small single-digit slice and now holds 30% of wafer revenue, and the company is telegraphing the same steepness for 2nm — CFO Wendell Huang explicitly guided Q3 to US$44.6-45.8 billion on "the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology," and the 2026 capital-spending plan was raised to US$60-64 billion, spending that only pays back if leading-edge output scales fast. The demand side is already committed: AI accelerator programs at NVIDIA and AMD, flagship smartphone silicon, and on-device NPU roadmaps all queue for the same leading-edge wafers, and TSMC describes demand as rationed by supply rather than by price. Within four reported quarters of its debut — that is, in the quarter ending June 2027 — 2nm should reach roughly a fifth of wafer revenue, displacing 3nm as the growth engine the same way 3nm displaced 5nm.

reasoning.because: TSMC's Q2 2026 report shows 2nm at 3% of wafer revenue in its debut quarter of a record period
reasoning.given: Q3 guidance leans on a steep 2nm ramp and 2026 capex was raised to US$60-64B to scale that node
reasoning.so_that: 2nm follows 3nm's ramp curve and crosses 20% of wafer revenue within four reported quarters of debut
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; TSMC quarterly report discloses 2nm at 20% or more of wafer revenue
reasoning.plain_language: TSMC's newest chip process just earned its first revenue; if it grows like the previous generation, it becomes a fifth of sales within a year.

predictions.summary: TSMC's record Q2 2026 showed 2nm contributing 3% of wafer revenue in its debut quarter, with Q3 guidance built on a steep 2nm ramp and capex raised to US$60-64B. Following the adoption curve 3nm traced to its current 30% share, 2nm is predicted to reach 20% of wafer revenue by Q2 2027.
